Inline comments:
In `@internal/restapi/arrivals_and_departures_for_stop_handler.go`:
- Around line 290-304: Update the per-arrival BuildTripStatus flow to consume
the existing request-scoped freqMap instead of calling GetFrequenciesForTrip for
each arrival. Thread the batched frequency records through BuildTripStatus or
its surrounding cache, preserving the first ordered frequency for each trip and
eliminating all N individual lookups after GetFrequenciesForTrips.

In `@internal/restapi/schedule_for_stop_handler.go`:
- Around line 169-172: The frequency lookup handling in the schedule-for-stop
handler must stop returning a successful response when GetFrequenciesForTrips
fails. In the freqErr branch, pass freqErr to api.serverErrorResponse and return
immediately; retain the existing not-found handling only where errors.Is(err,
sql.ErrNoRows) applies.
- Around line 566-572: Update frequencyVoteWeight to check freq.HeadwaySecs <= 0
and return weight 1 before calculating the division; retain the existing
nonpositive computed-weight fallback for valid headways.

In `@internal/restapi/trip_for_vehicle_handler.go`:
- Around line 119-125: Propagate GetFrequenciesForTrip database errors instead
of treating them as absent frequencies: in
internal/restapi/trip_for_vehicle_handler.go:119-125 return serverErrorResponse
for non-sql.ErrNoRows failures; in internal/restapi/trips_helper.go:159-163
propagate the error through BuildTripStatus, at 387-390 return it from
frequencyForEntry, and at 440-444 return it from BuildTripSchedule. Only
successful empty results may produce a nil frequency; handle sql.ErrNoRows with
sendNotFound and all other errors as HTTP 500.

In `@internal/restapi/trips_for_location_handler.go`:
- Around line 378-390: After a successful batch query, initialize every trip key
in the frequency map to nil before appending returned rows, so trips without
frequencies are cached and do not trigger fallback queries. Apply this in
internal/restapi/trips_for_location_handler.go lines 378-390 around the
validVehicleTrips batch flow, and in internal/restapi/trips_for_route_handler.go
lines 326-344 around the fetched trip IDs; leave each map empty when the batch
query fails.

please fix the items noted in the inline review and we'll get this merged!

Reviewed against legacy Java (pinned at the SHA the wiki already cites) and the codebase's own conventions, alongside @aaronbrethorst's review and an independent `/code-review` pass. Most of CodeRabbit's earlier actionable comments on this PR (N+1 caching, division-by-zero guard, error propagation in several handlers, the routeDirection key-type refactor, missing doc comments) are already fixed in the current HEAD and don't need further action — I re-verified each against the code rather than trusting the stale comment text.

Two spec-conformance items came out of comparing against legacy Java source:

1. **Frequency window selection always picks the first `frequencies.txt` row for a trip, not the one matching the request time** (see inline comment on `frequencyForEntry`). Legacy Java resolves the time-matching `FrequencyEntry` per request; this PR's `frequencyForEntry`/`freqs[0]` shortcuts don't. This needs fixing — see inline comment.
2. **`schedule-for-stop` expanding `exact_times=1` trips into discrete `scheduleStopTimes`** deviates from legacy Java, which lumps all frequency trips (`exact_times` 0 or 1) into `scheduleFrequencies` undifferentiated. We've decided to keep this behavior — it's a defensible improvement (GTFS's `exact_times=1` semantics call for exact timetable-equivalent output, and schedule-for-stop's underlying Java bean has no `exactTimes` field to fall back on, unlike the `frequency` object elsewhere). This has been documented in the `maglev.wiki` `schedule-for-stop` page's Implementation Decisions section — no action needed here, just flagging so the intentional divergence is visible in-PR too.

The rest are correctness/consistency findings from combining @aaronbrethorst's review with an independent `/code-review medium` pass — each verified against current HEAD and confirmed still applicable.
